newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa ends down after bumping resistance.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa ends down after bumping resistance.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa futures closed lower across the board on Friday, with benchmark May losing a battle to conquer nearby resistance around 1,040 stg.
The market started firmer after New York's strong performance on Thursday, and May moved up to 1,040 to test resistance.
But origin sales were said to have limited gains and by afternoon May started showing some fatigue and backed off, ending down 15 stg at 1,016 stg per tonne, just off its intraday low of 1,013.
Light volumes also exaggerated moves and made cocoa's next direction blurry, traders said.
"The volume is very light. So, therefore, it was really...very volatile because it was pushed up in no volume, pushed down in no volume," a trader said.
"To be quite honest, I'm a bit lost here. At the end of the week, it's such light volume, it's very difficult to tell (which way cocoa will move next)."
Total volume was a very modest 3,519 lots, mostly on tbe second-month May.
Traders said although the market seemed to want to edge higher, overbought RSI levels and stochastics were pointing the market lower.

They also looked for clues in the fundamentals to justify higher prices. Dry weather in Ivory Coast caused some nervousness but traders were uncertain if this would seriously affect the development of the mid-crop.
Crop analysts in Abidjan said on Friday the Ivory Coast's mid-crop cocoa harvest was likely to exceed 100,000 tonnes while rain could boost it to 160,000 tonnes or more.
Some crop experts had said earlier this week that the mid-crop could be as low as 100,000 because of unusually dry weather.
Earlier on Friday, Brazilian Trade Commission Comcauba said Bahia cocoa arrivals were 9,791 bags in the week ending March 16, down from 13,887 bags in the corresponding week last year.
Arrivals for the 1997/97 crop-to-date were 2,803,033 bags, up from 2,582,155 bags in 1995/96, it added.
